node.statement: Use only the validated premises 1.1.2, 1.3.1, and 1.3.2. Insert P_n(XQ_n) and P_nX, and use linearity of Y mapsto P_nY to obtain ||Co_{P_n,Q_n}(X)-X|| <= ||Co_{P_n,Q_n}(X)-P_n(XQ_n)|| + ||P_n(XQ_n-X)|| + ||P_nX-X||. Node 1.1.2 bounds the first term by k_co e||X|| and gives ||P_n||<=B and e_0<=1/2; nodes 1.3.2 and 1.3.1 respectively give ||XQ_n-X||<=Le||X|| and ||P_nX-X||<=Le||X||. Since epsilon<=e<=e_0<=1/2, submultiplicativity yields ||P_n(XQ_n-X)|| <= (1+epsilon)||P_n||||XQ_n-X|| <= 2BL e||X||. Consequently the displayed sum is at most [k_co+(2B+1)L]e||X||. With B=3 and finite universal k_co,L, C_ac:=k_co+(2B+1)L is finite universal, and e_ac:=e_0>0 is universal.
node.inference: triangle inequality, linearity, and submultiplicativity from validated premises
